name: Jarama bridges: Pindoque & Arganda
story: The Nationalist offensive of February 1937 needed to cross the Jarama. On the night of 11 February, Moroccan Regulares crept up to the Pindoque railway bridge near Vaciamadrid and silently killed the International Brigade sentries; a Republican attempt to blow the bridge failed, and it survived the explosion. Further south, Barrón's cavalry seized the Arganda road bridge. These crossings opened the way to the hills of Pingarrón and Suicide Hill. Nearby, on the Cerro del Melero at Rivas, stretches of Republican trenches from 1938 have been restored.
see: The railway bridge (rebuilt) and old Arganda road bridge over the Jarama in the Parque Regional del Sureste; restored trenches on the Cerro del Melero.
plan: Reach on foot or by bike from the Laguna del Campillo (Rivas-Vaciamadrid) along the river paths; free.
